react_result.final_narrative_text: Four independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this dataset. Across RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring, tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380 / hsa00380; WP:WP465) ranks #1 with FDR as low as 1.5e-14 and fold-enrichment exceeding 1,000x. The six confirmed driver metabolites span three branches of the tryptophan catabolic network: the serotonin/melatonin biosynthetic arm (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin via TPH1/2 and ASMT; R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.5e-08), the kynurenine-QUIN arm (L-tryptophan → N-formylkynurenine → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid via IDO1/TDO and KYNU; WP:WP5414, FDR 1.4e-08), and the direct tryptamine shunt (L-tryptophan → tryptamine via DDC). L-Leucine and putrescine appear only in secondary, marginally-significant leucine biosynthesis and urea-cycle hits (p ≥ 0.04), consistent with background amino-acid pool perturbation rather than specific pathway activation. The convergence of ORA (compound set overlap), KEGG PSEA (pathway topology), and mummichog (empirical m/z network) across independent metabolite lists strongly implicates systemic tryptophan catabolism reprogramming, with implications for neuroimmune signaling (serotonin/melatonin) and NAD+ biosynthetic capacity (quinolinic acid → NAD+ via QPRT).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis—all converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed network. RaMP ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" (FDR 1.5e-14, 6 metabolites hit) as the top pathway, with WP:WP4210 "Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production" (FDR 1.1e-10) capturing the kynurenine branch and REACT:R-HSA-209931 "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (FDR 3.5e-08) capturing the biogenic amine branch. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00380 as the top KEGG hit (p=1.03e-06, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog identifies MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its top pathway (p=0.0024, 12 matched network nodes). The driver set comprises L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632), all confirmed as members of the RaMP-enumerated KEGG:map00380 metabolite roster. All 9 input compounds resolved to distinct InChIKey first blocks with no structural conflicts.
